A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have attempted to show that the language practices of adult immigrant students in the ESL classroom can be seen to be constituting both the subjectivities of language learner and the object of language itself, and that the research practices used by second language researchers can be understood as contributing to the same processes.
the classroom interactions and research practices used to explore them are constitutive actions that produce particular social realities and subjectivities.
the theory of performativity provides us with a useful lens through which to view the complex interplay between language and social reality.
The main takeaway from our work is that

performativity theory provides a way of thinking about how language is constituted in social interaction, as well as a way of considering how language and subjectivity are constituted in research practices.

performativity theory offers a way for researchers to examine how the very practices of language learning and language learning research are implicated in the construction and reproduction of the social worlds we study.

performativity theory enables researchers to understand how the language practices of adult learners are not only about learning, but also about the production of social realities and subjectivities, and the ideological effects of such production.
